PIP & No-Fault Billing

Coverage Rules That Change at Every State Line

Personal Injury Protection, or PIP, is auto insurance coverage that pays medical bills after an accident regardless of who was at fault, and No-Fault billing is the broader system built around that coverage. Unlike MVA claims that wait on a legal settlement, PIP claims are usually billed and paid faster, directly through the auto insurer, but the rules governing coverage limits, required forms and filing deadlines differ meaningfully from state to state.

New York's no-fault system, for example, has its own specific forms, timely filing deadlines and dispute resolution process that differ from Florida's PIP statute or Michigan's no-fault framework. A biller unfamiliar with a specific state's requirements can easily file the wrong form, miss a deadline, or misunderstand a coverage limit, all of which delay or reduce payment.

PMEX bills PIP and no-fault claims according to each state's specific requirements, tracks coverage limits and deadlines by policy, and follows up with the auto insurer directly so claims move through the no-fault system as fast as that system allows.

How Coverage Differs by State

Three Frameworks, Three Different Playbooks

New York No-Fault

Specific state forms, defined timely filing deadlines, and a formal dispute resolution process through the state's no-fault arbitration system.

Florida PIP

A statutory framework with its own coverage percentage rules and required notice provisions specific to Florida's PIP statute.

Michigan No-Fault

A distinct no-fault framework with its own reimbursement fee schedule and coverage election structure.

Common Filing Mistakes We Prevent

Small Errors That Cost Real Money

Wrong State Form

Using a generic claim form instead of the state's required no-fault filing form.

Missed Filing Deadline

Filing after the state's specific timely submission window has closed.

Coverage Limit Miscalculation

Billing past the policy's remaining PIP limit without a plan for the balance.

Missed Dispute Window

Failing to challenge a denial within the state's required arbitration or appeal period.

PIP & No-Fault Billing: Frequently Asked Questions

PIP refers to the specific insurance coverage that pays medical bills after an accident regardless of fault. No-Fault is the broader legal and billing system built around that coverage, including the state-specific forms and processes used to bill it.

No-fault claims are typically much faster than liability-based claims, since they're paid directly by the auto insurer rather than waiting on a legal settlement, though exact timelines depend on the state's specific processing requirements.

Once a policy's PIP limit is exhausted, remaining charges may need to be pursued through the patient's health insurance or a liability claim, depending on the case and applicable state rules. PMEX tracks limits closely to flag this transition early.

Yes. PMEX bills PIP and no-fault claims according to each state's specific requirements, including New York, Florida, Michigan and other no-fault or PIP jurisdictions.

Denials are pursued through each state's specific dispute resolution process, whether that's a formal arbitration system or another required appeal path.
